key_insight: Deep-learning emulators can faithfully and stably replace a complex marine biogeochemistry model over both days-to-decades horizons, while sometimes improving forecast skill.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a path to much cheaper operational ocean prediction and climate-scale ecosystem simulation, with potential use in forecasting systems and autonomous marine platforms.
method: LSTM emulator for selected variables at daily resolution
Physics-informed 1D CNN emulator for the full water-column pelagic system
Driven by ocean physics simulator inputs and tested on short-range and multi-decadal forecasts
evidence_signal: The emulators were evaluated against the parent model on daily variability, extreme events, decadal climate projections, and 10-day forecasts, and when trained on reanalysis data they outperformed the parent model for several ecosystem variables.
watch_item: Results are demonstrated in a simplified 1D water-column setting, so performance may not transfer directly to full 3D regional or global ocean applications.
paper_title: Deep learning model emulators for marine biogeochemistry forecasting from days to decades
